title: Subjective risk Assessment in patients with acute chest pain compared with objective risk stratification and clinical outcomes
summary:
Chest pain is a common reason for presentation to an emergency department. For affected patients, it can be difficult to judge whether their symptoms are harmless or indicate a serious heart condition. At the same time, physicians assess the risk based on the symptoms, existing risk factors, and findings from routine medical examinations.

This study investigates how patients with acute chest pain assess their own health risk and how this assessment relates to the medical risk assessment and the subsequent clinical course.

Adults presenting to the Emergency Department of Marburg University Hospital with acute chest pain not caused by injury may participate. After written informed consent, participants complete a short questionnaire about how they perceive the cause and severity of their symptoms. In addition, data from routine medical care are evaluated. The subsequent health course is assessed approximately 30 days after the initial presentation. No additional examinations or treatments are performed for study purposes.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Acute non-traumatic chest pain
- Presentation to the Emergency Department of Marburg University Hospital
- Capacity to provide informed consent
- Written informed consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
- ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction requiring immediate intervention
- Acute life-threatening condition or medical instability
- Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
- Traumatic chest pain
- Language barriers precluding adequate informed consent or completion of the questionnaire
- Declined participation
